component.name: AppAttic
component.summary: Leftovers, stale apps, unused packages, and disk usage

description.p: AppAttic finds leftover data from uninstalled apps, unused installed software, unused distro and language packages, outdated versions, and large folders. Nothing is deleted until you review a script or confirm in the window. Disk usage can move a folder to Trash after you confirm.
The Linux window is Qt 6. Package-manager queries run on the host when installed as a Flatpak (flatpak-spawn --host). Named package updates wait for confirm. Full distro upgrades are not run.

A flag that names one command is now a usage error on every other one instead of a silent no-op. Put --leftovers-only and --stale-only after report, --allocated and --all-file-systems after disk, --top N after report, leftovers or disk, --category after report or leftovers, and --include-system, --fresh and --dry-run after the commands appattic --help lists. --yes still belongs to update alone. A script that passed one of these to a command that ignored it used to exit 0 and now exits 2, so move the flag to the command it names. A bare appattic --allocated is one of those: with the command left out the default is report, so name disk.
--category takes one value and is repeated, so --category caches browser is a usage error where it used to filter on both. Pass --category caches --category browser.

--version used to print the version and exit 0 even when the rest of the line was wrong, and --help lost to it. It now reports the usage error and exits 2, and --help wins, so appattic --version --help prints the help. appattic help [command] is new as a word: appattic help disk prints what appattic disk --help prints. With several wrong tokens on one line, the first one is the error reported.

appattic update asks on a terminal and stops with exit 2 when there is none, unless the run passes --yes. A cancelled update exits 1, where it used to exit 0. A disk path that is not a readable directory is a usage error rather than an empty report. An upgrade script that is still running after ten minutes is stopped and reported as exit 124, where it used to wait for the package manager to finish.
appattic config is new. It scans nothing: it prints the settings file this machine resolved, whether it exists, every setting with the layer it came from, and the paths the XDG variables resolved to.

An ignored leftover path in settings.json has to be the full path a report prints. A relative one, a ~ one, or one with a trailing slash matched nothing and hid nothing, so it is refused now, with the offending entry named: the CLI exits 2 and both windows open with no settings and say which entry to fix. The file is left exactly as it is, so correcting that one entry is the whole fix. The Linux window likewise no longer overwrites old settings that are neither true nor false with the defaults. It names the key and the old settings file, and opens with no settings until that file is corrected, because saving the defaults over your value would destroy it.

Generated cleanup scripts quote plugin names and paths, and a name containing a newline can no longer inject shell. Each package removal is now guarded by a check that the package is still there, so running a script twice no longer fails on what the first run removed, and only the part of a command that needs root asks for it. Your home path is redacted from error and status messages. Non-ASCII names, case folding, and date, size, and duration formatting follow the locale, which replaces the English today and 3 days ago and the yyyy-MM-dd date with your locale's own. The last-scan cache records the exact mtime of what it scanned, is dropped after a run that removes or updates something, and is dropped once it is over 24 hours old. A scan in which any check ran and failed is not saved, so a failed package query is retried on the next run instead of being served as "no unused packages" for a day.

A folder size could read smaller than it is: du exits non-zero when a path it was asked about failed, and a batched run counted the partial total it still printed as a real measurement. A bind mount that loops back into its own tree also spun the walk out to its deadline instead of finishing. Both are fixed, and Java, Gradle, Maven, and .m2 are recognized as system paths, so they are no longer offered as leftovers. Disk usage ranks the entries in each folder by the size it prints, by apparent size unless --allocated asked for allocated blocks, so --top N no longer cuts the wrong rows.

A PPA entry whose name was not a plain file name could put a path outside /etc/apt/sources.list.d into a generated cleanup script. Such a name is refused now, alongside the newline-injection fix above.
The Linux window ships a man page: man appattic-qt.
The AppImage ran only on the machine that built it: the bundled wasmtime recorded an absolute build path as its dependency, so a downloaded AppImage failed to start anywhere else.
Findings, disk folders, and the disk ring now appear as each plugin reports instead of after the whole scan finishes.
A date or version that cannot be read shows as unknown rather than an empty value.
The findings table is painted from a model rather than rebuilt, a rescan that returns the same findings no longer rebuilds it, and column widths are sampled instead of measured for every row.
Scans reuse the compiled WASM module and the wasmtime compilation cache across runs, a first scan starts faster, and a rescan saves about 60 ms.
The results table fills in roughly half the time, and search and filter toggles show or hide rows instead of rebuilding them.
Package-manager queries run in parallel, the byte-scan parsers were rewritten, and the grouping and probe fixes land with search debounce and the audit cleanups.
Disk usage builds on macOS again.
Disk usage, Linux distro cleanup, and portable package support.
The cache is invalidated after a same-name app update or a clock rollback, Homebrew cleanup is safe to rerun, and home paths no longer leak into generated scripts.
The offscreen Qt platform plugin is now shipped inside the AppImage, so every page renders without a display server.
First release: the Linux Qt window packaged as an AppImage, and the appattic scan CLI behind it.
